summary: DHCPv6 lease-renewal race on Windows creates ephemeral virtual adapter; Zero-trust agent binds to wrong interface and internal APIs fail
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (internal employees) intermittently lose access to internal APIs and services after a short period on corporate Wi-Fi. Symptoms correlate with Windows 11 clients that have both a wireless adapter and an on-host virtual network interface (Hyper-V / WSL2 / VPN virtual NICs).

Impact:
- Affects ~8-15% of roaming laptop population in us-east office over last 48 hours.
- Internal services (console, vault proxy, internal artifact registry) return connection errors despite VPN tunnel being up.
- Leads to SSO token refresh failures and developer productivity loss.

High level: DHCPv6 renewal (short lifetime) on the SSID causes Windows to momentarily create an ephemeral virtual adapter entry with the corporate DNS suffix. The Zero-trust agent chooses that interface (based on suffix match + lowest metric) and binds its control/egress to it. That adapter has no working default route to the corporate subnet, so traffic to internal APIs is blackholed while the user still shows as connected to VPN.

Observed start time: 2026-03-12 09:10 UTC (first internal report). Correlated with Meraki MR firmware 1.14.5 deployment and a staged Windows 11 HA update (KB-2026-01) rolled this week.

Notes: This ticket is internal-only investigation; customer-facing support unaffected.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Worker laptop (Win11) connects to corporate SSID and authenticates via 802.1X/OKTA.
2) Zero-trust agent establishes control plane and creates VPN tunnel over primary wireless interface.
3) After ~10-30 minutes DHCPv6 rapid-renewal is seen (DHCPv6 IA_NA lease with short preferred lifetime).
4) Windows transiently registers an ephemeral virtual interface entry with the same DNS suffix (observed as 'vEthernet (WSL)' or similar).
5) Zero-trust agent picks the ephemeral interface for flow egress due to suffix match + lower metric, binds socket there, and traffic to internal endpoints fails despite tunnel up.
6) Reverting the interface metric or disabling the ephemeral interface restores connectivity until next renewal.

Zero-trust agent debug (2026-03-13T09:22:15Z): Selected egress interface 'vEthernet (WSL)' for route rule match {dns_suffix: 'redwood.internal', metric: 5} — opening control socket on 172.31.240.15 (no route to internal API 10.10.5.20).
Windows System Event: NetworkListManager: Network profile changed: DomainNetwork -> Private (ephemeral interface added).
tcpdump on gateway (sw-us-east-01): no packets from client to internal API while VPN tunnel signals active (IKE keepalive present).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 10:00 - Maya: Reproduced locally on test laptop. Forced DHCPv6 renewal via 'ipconfig /renew6' triggered ephemeral adapter entry. Verified DNS suffix match and wrong metric selection causing ZTA to bind incorrectly.

2026-03-13 10:25 - Julian: Pulled ZTA debug logs — agent chooses egress based on suffix and 'best metric' heuristic. Heuristic didn't account for 'has default gateway' flag. Logged edge case for engineering.

2026-03-13 11:05 - NetInfra (Priya): Checked Meraki MR firmware rollouts — release 1.14.5 introduced shorter DHCPv6 preferred lifetime auto-config for RA/DHCPv6 in our profile. Suspicion: RA/DHCPv6 change triggers more frequent re-registration events on clients.

2026-03-13 11:40 - Endpoint (Sam): WSL and Hyper-V virtual adapters on Windows will re-register DNS when the DHCPv6 client updates leases, creating ephemeral entries with same DNS suffix but no default gateway. We saw identical behavior in an internal lab when DHCPv6 lease preferred lifetime set <120s.

2026-03-13 12:15 - Support: Scoped affected population and started pilot config to raise DHCPv6 preferred lifetime on SSID to 7200s for us-east. Also pushed temporary Intune configuration to set interface metric for virtual adapters to 5000 (lower priority).
2026-03-13 15:00 - Monitoring: After changes, incidents on the pilot subset dropped to 0.9% from 12% baseline.
comments: Maya Patel (Support) - 2026-03-13T10:05: 'Repro'd on lab Win11 image; ephemeral adapter gets DNS suffix and ZTA picks it. Captured ipconfig and agent trace. Attaching to this ticket.'

Julian Reed (SRE) - 2026-03-13T10:28: 'Agent's egress selection relies on dns_suffix match *and then* metric. It doesn't currently validate that interface has a usable default route. Adding a check would be low-risk. Logging an engineering ticket.'
Priya Shah (NetInfra) - 2026-03-13T11:12: 'Meraki MR profile change noted; rolling back DHCPv6 preferred lifetime to 2h for us-east SSID as experiment. Observed fewer reoccurrences in pilot.'
Sam Torres (Endpoint) - 2026-03-13T12:20: 'Intune policy prepared to set high metric on vEthernet/WSL adapters (5000). Will schedule rollout to affected OUs. This is a bandaid until agent fix ships.'

Julian Reed (SRE) - 2026-03-14T08:00: 'Created ENG-8271 to add interface route validation to egress selection. Proposed check: interface must advertise default gateway OR have active route to 10.0.0.0/8 before binding. Punted to next sprint but patch candidate available for hotfix.'
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: NetInfra rolled DHCPv6 preferred lifetime back to 7200s on corporate SSID, and Endpoint pushed Intune config to raise metric for virtual adapters. Incidents in pilot region dropped to baseline. Engineering task (ENG-8271) opened to harden Zero-trust agent egress logic to verify route viability before binding; target hotfix planned for 2026-03-22. Postmortem draft assigned to Maya for 2026-03-17.
next_steps: 1) ENG to prioritize ENG-8271: add 'has default route' check and unit tests for egress selection. Target hotfix 2026-03-22.
2) NetInfra to monitor global Meraki rollout and prevent DHCPv6 life changes without canarying.
3) Endpoint to roll Intune metric tweak to remaining OUs if hotfix delayed beyond 2026-03-22.
4) Run 72h verification job to confirm incidents remain <1% in all regions.
